newsitem.title: USA: Bliley says U.S. electric reform a priority.
newsitem.headline: Bliley says U.S. electric reform a priority.

text.p: Commerce Committee Chairman Thomas Bliley said deregulation of the electricity industry would be a top priority next session if Republicans retained control of the House in the November elections.
Bliley also said the committee would try again to pass legislation to modify the Superfund law for cleaning up toxic waste and push for reform of the Food and Drug Administration.
"I'm confident that we'll get FDA and Superfund, also we want to give people a choice in electricity, not just companies but individuals as well," Bliley told reporters.
He predicted a lot of "twists and turns" and hearings in the push to deregulate the electricity industry, but said he was confident a solution could be found.

Bliley said the first priority of any deregulatory effort would be to ensure that individuals and small businesses got cost savings, not just big business. He also said states and the FERC would have to be involved to ensure that the effort was uniform and coordinated.
